answers: It trembles and is moved out of its place
easy.explanation: Elihu says, “my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.”
easy.q: What happens to Elihu’s heart at the storm?

easy.explanation: The passage speaks of “the sound that goeth out of his mouth.”
easy.q: What goes out of God’s mouth?

easy.explanation: The text says, “God thundereth marvellously with his voice.”
easy.q: What does God do with his voice?

answers: Under the whole heaven and unto the ends of the earth
medium.explanation: God directs it “under the whole heaven” and unto the ends of the earth.
medium.q: Where does God direct his lightning?

medium.explanation: After it, “a voice roareth,” and He thunders with the voice of His excellency.
medium.q: What follows the sound of God’s voice?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes God’s majestic greatness and power.
medium.q: What does “his excellency” mean in this passage?

answers: It is presented as an expression of His powerful voice
It proves that people control nature
challenge.explanation: Thunder is described as God’s voice and as part of His marvelous works.
challenge.q: How does the thunder relate to God’s greatness?

answers: Some of God’s works are beyond human understanding
God does not work in the world
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the limits of human understanding.
challenge.q: What does “which we cannot comprehend” suggest?

challenge.explanation: The trembling heart and the mighty thunder suggest awe, fear, and wonder.
challenge.q: What central feeling arises from the description of God’s voice?

paragraphs.title: Snow, Rain, and the Forces of Nature

easy.explanation: God says to the snow, “Be thou on the earth.”
easy.q: What does God say to the snow?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Then the beasts go into dens.”
The text says, “By the breath of God frost is given.”
easy.q: What is given by the breath of God?

answers: It seals up his hand so that he may know God’s work
It makes him rule the clouds
It prevents him from seeing the earth
medium.explanation: God “sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.”
medium.q: What effect does God’s work have on every man?

answers: He closes or restrains the hand
He strengthens the hand for battle
He hides the hand from sight
medium.explanation: The phrase pictures God stopping human activity so people may recognize His work.
medium.q: What does “sealeth up” mean in this context?

answers: For correction, for the land, or for mercy
medium.explanation: God causes the weather to come “whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.”
medium.q: For what purposes may the clouds be sent?

answers: The beasts enter dens and remain in their places
The storm has no effect on them
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the weather with the beasts’ retreat into their dens.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the storm and the beasts?

answers: As things directed by God’s command
challenge.explanation: The weather is repeatedly described as responding to God’s will and command.
challenge.q: How are rain, snow, frost, and clouds presented?

answers: Nature always affects people in exactly the same way
God may use it for judgment, benefit, or mercy
challenge.explanation: The verse presents several possible purposes, including correction and mercy.
challenge.q: What does “whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy” imply?

paragraphs.title: A Call to Contemplate God’s Wonders

easy.explanation: Elihu says, “Hearken unto this, O Job.”
Job is told to stand still and consider God’s wondrous works.
easy.q: What does Job receive a command to consider?

easy.explanation: The passage asks whether God caused “the light of his cloud to shine.”

medium.explanation: Elihu twice asks Job, “Dost thou know?” about God’s works and the clouds.
medium.q: What question is repeated in verses 15–16?

answers: The way the clouds are arranged or suspended
medium.explanation: The expression refers to the ordered arrangement or movement of the clouds.
medium.q: What are the “balancings of the clouds”?

answers: People are limited in knowledge, while God’s works are wondrous
People control the heavens, while God watches
People and God possess equal power
medium.explanation: Elihu’s questions highlight Job’s limited understanding of God’s works.
medium.q: What contrast appears between God and humanity?

answers: He is invited to pause and observe God’s works
He is commanded to leave the earth
He is told to hide from the clouds
challenge.explanation: The command directs Job’s attention toward careful contemplation of God’s wonders.
challenge.q: Why is Job told to “stand still, and consider”?

challenge.explanation: The comparison presents the sky as strong, solid, and mirror-like.
challenge.q: What does the comparison to a “molten looking glass” suggest about the sky?

answers: Job can explain every work of God
Job must recognize the limits of his understanding
challenge.explanation: The questions lead Job to acknowledge that God’s works exceed human knowledge.
challenge.q: What is the main message of Elihu’s questions?

answers: What they should say unto God
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Teach us what we shall say unto him.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask others to teach him?

easy.explanation: They cannot order their speech “by reason of darkness.”
easy.q: Why can people not order their speech?

easy.explanation: The text says, “the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.”

answers: Properly order their speech or hide their words
See the bright light in the clouds
medium.explanation: The passage stresses that people cannot order their speech before God and cannot escape His notice.
medium.q: What can human beings not do before God?

answers: Arrange or present our words properly
medium.explanation: The phrase means to arrange or present an argument in an orderly way.
The wind passes and cleanses the clouds, allowing the bright light to be seen.
medium.q: What happens when the wind passes through the clouds?

answers: It prevents people from properly ordering their words before God
It gives people power over God
It proves that no light exists
challenge.explanation: Darkness is given as the reason people cannot order their speech before God.
challenge.q: How is darkness connected with human limitation?

answers: Light may exist even when clouds temporarily conceal it
Light is made only by people
challenge.explanation: The bright light is present in the clouds but becomes visible when the wind clears them.
challenge.q: What does the hidden light teach about God’s creation?

answers: People can argue with God without limits
People are limited before God and cannot hide from Him
People understand all the works of the clouds
challenge.explanation: Both verses emphasize human inability to speak adequately before God or escape His notice.
challenge.q: What common idea appears in verses 19–20?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Fair weather cometh out of the north.”
God is described as excellent “in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice.”
The passage concludes, “Men do therefore fear him.”
easy.q: What should men do because of God’s majesty?

answers: Because He has terrible majesty and is excellent in power, judgment, and justice
Because He does not work in the world
Because He depends on human wisdom
medium.explanation: God’s majesty and excellence in power, judgment, and justice give reason for reverence.
The phrase describes majesty that inspires awe and reverence.

answers: God does not respect them merely for their wisdom
medium.explanation: The final verse says that God “respecteth not any that are wise of heart.”
medium.q: What is said about those who are wise in heart?

answers: Both the weather and the radiance reveal God’s majestic power
The weather proves that God is weak
challenge.explanation: The changing heavens point to God’s greatness and inspire awe.
challenge.q: How does the description of fair weather connect with the storm passages?

answers: It says God acts only with power
It shows that God’s greatness includes abundant justice
It says God ignores human actions
challenge.explanation: The phrase joins abundant justice with God’s power and judgment.
challenge.q: What does “in plenty of justice” add to the description of God?

answers: Human wisdom can require God to explain Himself
Even the wise cannot demand that God justify Himself
challenge.explanation: The conclusion teaches that human wisdom does not place God under obligation.
challenge.q: What is the final relationship between human wisdom and God?
